transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Well, I'm here because for months now, I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern in my project files. Certain subcontractors and one colleague in particular keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. They're doing it so it looks like my quality control failed. And... even when IT looks at it and says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
When IT showed you the audit trail was clean, what did you think was happening — do you think they made a mistake, or is there another explanation for why the records appeared clean to them?

Well, like I said, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. I don't think IT made a mistake, exactly... they're just looking at the surface level with their standard checks. 

But this colleague and the subcontractors, they know the translation memory software inside and out. They know exactly how to make those tiny changes to the timestamps in a way that doesn't trigger the system's security flags. So when IT pulls the logs, of course it appears clean to them. But I work with these files every single day. I know what the original segments looked like, and I know what I'm seeing now. The pattern is definitely there, even if IT's software doesn't catch it.
Have you directly confronted this colleague or the subcontractors about these changes you've noticed, or reported this pattern to your manager or HR?

Well, I haven't formally gone to HR or anything like that. I haven't lost my job, and I haven't missed any major deadlines over this. 

But I have brought it up with the team. Project meetings have gotten... pretty tense, honestly, because I keep pressing for the record to be corrected. I just want the files to reflect what actually happened. Because of that, I've noticed a few of my colleagues, um... they kind of avoid looping me into routine discussions now, unless they absolutely have to.

When IT showed you those clean audit trails, did any part of you wonder if maybe you could be mistaken about the changes — or are you completely certain that the alterations are real, regardless of what the logs show?

No, I don't think I'm mistaken. I mean, like I've been saying, I've been tracking this exact same pattern in the project files for months now. I am completely certain the alterations are real. 

Even when IT tells me the audit trail is clean, I know for a fact the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. I do this for a living, so I know when the translation memory and the timestamps have been tweaked to make my quality control look like it failed. So, no, I don't really have any doubts about what that colleague and the subcontractors are doing, regardless of what the logs show.

If I were to tell you that multiple IT experts independently reviewed those same files and found no evidence of tampering, would that be possible to you — or do you think that scenario itself would be part of the arrangement to cover this up?

Honestly... if you told me multiple IT experts reviewed it and found nothing, I would just say they are missing it. I don't necessarily think the IT experts are part of some big cover-up, but they just don't see what I see. 

I mean, I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern in the project files. It's right there. Certain subcontractors and that one colleague keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps, and it's done specifically so it looks like my quality control failed. 

So, even if a dozen IT experts look at it and say the audit trail is clean, it doesn't change the reality of the files I work with. I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me, regardless of who reviews their logs.

Outside of work — in your personal life, with family, friends, or other situations — do you notice similar patterns of people arranging things against you, or is this mainly something you've experienced with this colleague and these subcontractors at work?

No, not at all. It's really just... it's just this specific situation at work. Outside of the project issue, everything is fine. I still do my regular translating, I manage my team’s workflow without any problems... um, I pay the bills, keep up with all my normal family routines. 

I don't have any issues with my friends or family, or anyone else trying to set me up. The only place things really go off track, or get stressful, is when the file history or those certain coworkers come up. Other than that, my life is completely normal.
